To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a recombinant adenovirus was constructed that expressed the bovine coronavirus haemagglutin-esterase glyco- protein and that the recombinantly expressed protein was antigenically and functionally indistinguishable from authentic bovine coronavirus haematglutinin- esterase glycoprotein.

we have constructed a recombinant adenovirus that directs the synthesis of bovine coronavirus haemagglutinesterase (HE) in mammalian cells, and that the recombinantly expressed HE polypeptide is glycosylated and is immunoreactive with conformation-specific monoclonal antibodies.
the bovine coronavirus HE gene, when expressed by recombinant adenovirus in vivo, is glycosylated and processed, and induces a specific antibody response in mice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an adenoviral vector that expresses a major viral glycoprotein of BCV.
the synthesis and processing of the BCV haemagglutinesterase glycoproteins encoded in the E 3 region of adenocarcinoma.
the synthesis and processing of the BCV haemagglutinesterase (HE) polypeptide encoded by an adenovirus recombinant.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the recombinants are able to direct synthesis of the BCVE polypeptide in vitro and in vivo.
the recombinants were capable of directing the expression of BCV HE protein in a form that was capable of inducing an antibody response.
recombinant Ad can serve as a potential vector for the expression of a foreign protein, and the recombinant protein can elicit a neutralizing antibody response.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the recombinants Ad5-HE and Ad5-BCV were successfully constructed and that the recombinantly expressed HE protein was processed and functional in vitro.
a recombinant Ad vector expressing the BCV HE gene is a potential live vaccine candidate for the prevention of BCV infection.
the HE gene of BCV is a useful candidate for inclusion into a vaccine vector for the induction of protective immunity against bovine coronavirus.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have demonstrated the ability to express a coronavirus HE protein in mammalian cells by the use of a recombinant adenovirus vector.
recombinant Ad can be used as a vector to direct the synthesis of foreign glycoproteins, which may be useful in the development of recombinant vaccines.
the recombinantly synthesized BCV HE polynucleotide can be expressed in a recombinant Ad vector and that the expressed BCV HE polypetide retains its antigenic and biological activities.
